summary: The draft is Boston Connor: short, stubborn, and absurd about real box scores. Three claims still miss the brief: Seattle-Denver is called Thursday, the Dak Side headline hangs 11.22 on the Elo lead, and “best running score” lands on Michael Mayer.

items.evidence: “Start your Patriots. I'm not asking.” “Write that down. It's the rule now.” “A Patriot was on the best lineup of the week. That's the reason. End of discussion.”

“Who the hell does that? At Gillette?” “Wake me when a Patriot does that here.” “The sponsor started Maye, four touchdown passes and a rushing score, and scored 177.00. That gets them seventh. Do it again.”
“Wake me when a Patriot does that here.” “Seventeen catches. A blowout. Pathetic.” “Best running score of the week. The margin was a rounding error. Still a loss.”
“Shough went 16 of 25 for 96 yards and two interceptions. … Score: minus 0.16. … A negative quarterback is correct if the other guy scores 69.56.”
“BENCHED. I don't care that they won by 74.92.” “Elo can live with it. I won't.” “Right total. Wrong bench. I'm still mad.” “The sponsor started Maye … That gets them seventh.”
“The name is a fraud. The win can stay.” “I'm still mad.” “Write that down. It's the rule now.” No wink and no walk-back.
“UNREAL.” “That's the job.” “Score: 0.00.” “Coin flip.” “New king.” “Ugly.” “Cardboard.” “Start Jefferson.”
The Shough stat line cuts to “A negative quarterback is correct if the other guy scores 69.56.” The Myers line cuts to “Print the kicker's name on the trophy.”
“Who the hell does that? At Gillette?” and “How do you lose that?” Two of them, both aimed at the manager.
“A kicker decided it.” “Points are a hobby.” “The back is the roster.” “It's the rule now.” The punchlines keep them as takes.
Two outbursts: “UNREAL.” in the lead and “BENCHED.” in recaps[1].
Maye's line stays flat, then “Who the hell does that?” Warren's line stays flat, then “BENCHED.”
“Embarrassing.” “Pathetic.” “Cardboard.” “Do it again.” “Start Jefferson.”
“Who the hell does that?” “Damn near a cliff from first to sixth.” “Write that down.” “I'm not asking.”
“hell” and “Damn” once each. Insults stay on lineups: “fraud,” “Embarrassing,” “Pathetic,” “disaster.”
Spread once each, not stacked: “fraud” (rankings[3]), “Unbelievable” (recaps[3]), “Embarrassing” (recaps[2]), “Pathetic” (recaps[1]), “disaster” (recaps[6]).
“a sneeze behind 1018.79.” “Damn near a cliff from first to sixth.” “The margin was a rounding error.” “Cardboard, not steel.”
Gillette, Foxborough, and the Patriots are the week's actual game. “Start Maye” in the preview follows the Jets at Gillette.
No polished transitions. Closers are “Lock the lineup up” energy: “End of discussion.” “The number is the number.” “Cardboard.”
“It's the rule now.” “I'm not asking.” “End of discussion.” “The back is the roster.”
“A negative quarterback is correct if the other guy scores 69.56.” “A Patriot was on the best lineup of the week. That's the reason.” Stevenson at 17.50, with Maye at 39.46 left out on purpose.
“Print the kicker's name on the trophy.” “Write that down. It's the rule now.” “Cardboard, not steel.”
“BENCHED.” “Who the hell does that?” “Right total. Wrong bench. I'm still mad.”
“A blowout. Pathetic.” “You picked wrong. Embarrassing.” “The lineup is a disaster. Cardboard.”
“I don't care that they won by 74.92.” “The name is a fraud. The win can stay.” “McVay said the kicking cost them the game. … You don't lose by 44.46 because of a kicker.”

items.evidence: “Seattle was at Denver on Thursday.” “Dak Side takes the top Elo spot by 11.22” “Michael Mayer started at superflex and caught 1 ball for 2 yards. Best running score in the league.”
“A kicker decided it. Print the kicker's name on the trophy.” “McVay said the kicking cost them the game” tracks the ESPN quote, then “You don't lose by 44.46 because of a kicker.”
Stat sentences stay straight: “Maye went 26 of 34 for 374 yards and four touchdowns.” “Puka Nacua caught 17 passes for 138 yards and a touchdown in the loss.”
Caps are “UNREAL.” and “BENCHED.” only. No short sentence is repeated. “Cardboard” echoes once, on the same team, and is not a second catchphrase.
Conviction, a Patriots grudge, and a straight stat line that snaps into a bad argument. “A negative quarterback is correct if the other guy scores 69.56. Write that down. It's the rule now.”

notes.quote: Seattle was at Denver on Thursday.
notes.problem: The week 6 schedule says “SEA at DEN (2026-10-16, Empower Field at Mile High).” Fetch day is Saturday 2026-10-17, so 2026-10-16 is Friday. The brief lists no Thursday game.

notes.quote: Dak Side takes the top Elo spot by 11.22
notes.problem: 11.22 is the score margin, 184.34 to 173.12. Elo has Dak Side at 1018.79 and hammball second at 1018.49, a gap of 0.30. The week's Elo change is +17.28. The headline puts the score margin on the ranking.
notes.fix: Keep 11.22 on the score. The body already does that with “Final gap, 11.22.” Don't attach it to the Elo spot.

notes.quote: Michael Mayer started at superflex and caught 1 ball for 2 yards. Best running score in the league.
notes.problem: Mayer's line is 1 catch for 2 yards, 1.20 points. The best running-back score is Jahmyr Gibbs at 37.70, on 25 carries for 151 yards and two touchdowns. The superlative sits on Mayer. It also can't mean rushing yards: Irving ran for 165.
notes.fix: Move “best running score” onto Gibbs and 37.70, right after his line and before Moore and Mayer.

notes.quote: Mendozareamazingpicks left 84.16 on the bench, the most, and still scored 226.24. Likely's 32.40 led every sit
notes.problem: 84.16 is Mendoza's bench total. Likely's 32.40 is the biggest single sit in the league, and he is on WELL! It's The Big Shough's bench. Mendoza's top sit is Jayden Daniels at 32.26. “led every sit” is true, and the missing team makes Likely read as part of the 84.16.
notes.fix: Name Big Shough in the Likely sentence.

notes.problem: The brief line is FG 5/5 (long 50), XP 2/2, and 23.00 is the whole kicking score. The take gives 23.00 to the field goals alone. The recap's “That's 23.00 from a kicker” is the accurate version.
notes.fix: Say he made 5 field goals, long of 50, and scored 23.00.

notes.quote: Missed Tampa's win with a thumb. Daniels started, per ESPN.
notes.problem: The Bucs recap's Daniels is Jalon Daniels, filling in for Baker Mayfield. Jayden Daniels played for Washington and is the quarterback benched in the Mendoza recap. The bare last name collides.
